title: Agentops decision record
description: One outcome of a planning or review cycle, classified before it can be emitted. The owner queue is built from these, not from prose. A derivable outcome is a resolution and never reaches the queue; an authorization gate is its own kind, because a refused tool call is a gate and not a deliberation; only ratification and new-value-choice records are decisions at all.

id.description: Stable id. Becomes a heading anchor and a queue key.

kind.description: The three axes, made into record kinds. 'resolution' is a derived answer and is not a decision; 'authorization' is a permission or acceptance gate and is not a deliberation; 'ratification' brings a resolved action for signature; 'new-value-choice' is the only real escalation.

claim.description: What is being asserted, in one sentence.

governing_refs.description: Where the rule actually is. A remembered scope is not a constraint, so a record cannot be emitted without at least one, and each must state the scope it was read as having -- that is the field the eight escalations of 2026-08-26 would each have had to fill in wrongly, in writing, to survive.

location.description: file:line, section reference, or numbered rule.

revision.description: The revision the text was read at, when it is known.

stated_scope.description: What the rule ranges over, in the rule's own terms: a class, a route, a kind, a window, a path.

unresolved_delta.description: What the governing text does not settle. Required for a new-value-choice: if nothing is left over, the answer was derivable.

authority_required.description: The authority the action needs. Required for ratification and authorization.

recommendation.description: The resolved action being brought for signature, or the reading being recommended.

resolved_action.description: What was done, for a resolution. A derivable outcome is reported as an action taken, not a question asked.

supersedes.description: Decision ids this record replaces. Corrections append; they never rewrite.
